summary:
All three HTML files are self-contained, fully-offline, single-file corpus preview dashboards for the RAG "content factory" — human QA/review viewers over extracted book content, with all data embedded as JSON constants in the page (no network calls). NONE of the three is the "Book Page View" per-page OCR verification dashboard (no PROBLEM_DENSE tags, no page-classification checklist, no raw OCR text view anywhere in these files) — that dashboard, if it exists, is a different file not present in docs/reference/.

preview-1.html (3.1MB, title "LRDI corpus preview", header "LRDI extraction — corpus preview") is the EARLIER, 4-book CAT/LRDI-only corpus preview generated from MASTER_corpus.jsonl: 2,052 records / 4,665 questions / 3,922 with answer key / 2,673 with solutions / 258 explainers / 14 errata adjudicated, covering Arun Sharma, Sinha, Thakur, Tyra. preview-2.html (8.4MB, same title, same app code) is the LATER, 9-book expanded version of the exact same dashboard, adding the GRE titles (ETS GRE, ETS GRE Verbal, Manhattan 5 lb, Manhattan Quant) and Lewis: 2,491 records / 7,667 questions / 6,802 keyed / 5,642 with solutions / 269 explainers / 14 errata adjudicated. Both share identical UI/JS: book chip buttons, book+chapter selects, full-text search, three toggle filters (errata only / unkeyed only / has stimulus), 20-records-per-page pager, inline SVG chart rendering of structured stimulus data (pie/bar/line drawn from the extracted numbers) plus a data-table rendering, per-question answer-key/derived-answer/errata/solution display. This is the "explore/enrichment corpus viewer" — it supports eyeballing extraction quality at the record level: which questions lack keys, which have errata, whether chart stimuli were transcribed into structured numeric form, and reading the notes field which records transcription provenance and book defects.

gre_preview.html (4.0MB, title "GRE corpus — questions and writing", header "GRE corpus") is a separate, later-styled dashboard (proper light/dark theming with data-theme override) dedicated to the 4 GRE books only. It has four tabs: Questions (262 sets / 3,002 questions, filters: book, chapter, search with <mark> highlight), Essay prompts (355 prompts — 192 Analyze an Argument + 163 Analyze an Issue, from the official ETS pool), Scored responses (59 sample essays with ETS reader commentary, filterable by task and score band 1-6), and Rubrics (7 scoring guides). Stats: 3,002 questions / 2,880 keyed / 2,969 with solutions / 0 flagged. Its per-question "v" field renders a "needs vision" flag — marking questions whose figures/options are raster images requiring a vision-model pass, which is the main open extraction gap it surfaces. It supports the GRE-content QA workflow: verifying question/key/solution completeness and reviewing the Analytical Writing assets (prompts deliberately NOT paired with scored responses — the UI states any pairing would be invented).

The data schemas embedded in these pages are the de-facto MASTER_corpus.jsonl schema and are the most concrete record of the extraction pipeline's output contract: records typed by content_type (question_set / explainer / essay_sample / reader_commentary / essay_prompt / scoring_guide / skip / front_matter / reference), question-level provenance fields (key_source, key_basis, derivation_note, unanswered_reason, errata adjudication states like CONFIRMED_BOOK_ERRATUM / PROVEN_WRONG), structured stimulus transcription (line_chart/bar_chart/pie_chart/table with actual numeric series), and explainer records with formula verification status.

workstream_notes.backend: These dashboards are read-only previews with no backend coupling, but they document the canonical corpus record shape the backend will ingest: records keyed by set_id with book/chapter/pdf_pages provenance, content_type discriminator, questions[] with answer_key + question_format + solution_note, and structured stimulus objects (charts as numeric series) that can be re-rendered client-side as SVG — meaning the app can render DI charts natively from data rather than serving page images. question_format taxonomy (multiple_choice, numeric_entry, short_answer, quantitative_comparison, multi_select, text_completion, select_in_passage, options_are_images) maps directly to the answer-input widgets the game server / apps must support.
workstream_notes.data_extraction: Central evidence of pipeline state. Corpus grew from 4 books/2,052 records/4,665 questions (preview-1) to 9 books/2,491 records/7,667 questions/6,802 keyed (preview-2), plus a GRE-only slice of 3,002 questions/2,880 keyed in gre_preview. Outstanding gaps quantified in-data: ~139 questions with unanswered_reason (raster-image options/stems needing a vision-model pass), 146 questions with figure.status='not_transcribed', 244 options_are_images + 459 unclassified formats, Sinha only 64% keyed, Lewis PDF never sourced. Quality mechanisms already in place: key_source/key_basis provenance strings, derived_answer with derivation_note (answers computed from chart data), errata adjudication (CONFIRMED_BOOK_ERRATUM / PROVEN_WRONG, 14 adjudicated), explainer formula verification (81 verified / 3 refuted). The expected 'Book Page View' OCR/page-classification (PROBLEM_DENSE) dashboard is NOT among these three files — these are all post-extraction corpus viewers; the page-level verification tool must be sought elsewhere or rebuilt. Note also the LRDI dashboards' 'errata only' filter bug (q._errata vs q.errata).
workstream_notes.rag: The corpus embedded here IS the content-factory output at snapshot time: 2,491 records across 9 books, including 269 structured explainers (technique/topic/definition/key_points/formulas/worked_example with verification flags) usable as teaching content for the app, and full solution prose on 5,642 questions usable for RAG-grounded explanations. GRE Analytical Writing assets (355 official-pool prompts, 59 ETS-scored sample essays with reader commentary across all 6 score bands, 7 rubrics) are a distinct content class for any writing-feedback feature — with the explicit caveat that prompts and scored samples are unpaired and must not be presented as pairs. Content-type taxonomy (question_set/explainer/essay_prompt/essay_sample/reader_commentary/scoring_guide/reference/skip/front_matter) is the enrichment classification the factory applies to book pages.

decisions_and_status: Confirmed: preview-1.html = earlier 4-book (CAT/LRDI + Vedic math) corpus preview; preview-2.html = same dashboard regenerated over the expanded 9-book corpus (adds 4 GRE books + Lewis); gre_preview.html = separate GRE-only 4-tab viewer covering questions plus Analytical Writing assets

Confirmed: none of the three files is the Book Page View / OCR page-classification (PROBLEM_DENSE) verification dashboard — that artifact is not in docs/reference/ and must be located elsewhere or rebuilt

Corpus status at snapshot: 2,491 records, 7,667 questions, 6,802 keyed (88.7%), 5,642 with solutions, 269 explainers, 14 errata adjudicated; GRE slice: 3,002 questions, 2,880 keyed, 2,969 solved, 0 flagged
